topic: Kimi K2.7-Code cuts thinking tokens 30% — but practitioners say the benchmarks don't check out

headline: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K2.7-Code with 30% less thinking tokens
summary: Kimi K2.7-Code claims 30% reduction in thinking tokens and improved performance
details: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code, an open-source update to its K2 coding model family, claiming leaner reasoning and double-digit performance gains. K2.7-Code is built on the same trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture as its predecessor K2.6.

K2.7-Code reduces thinking-token usage by 30% compared to K2.6, which would directly affect inference costs for teams running agentic workflows. The model is deployable via vLLM or SGLang and runs exclusively in thinking mode.

The core change from K2.6 is how the model generates low-level code. K2.7-Code authors implementations directly, producing more reliable generalization across Rust, Go and Python, and across task types including frontend development, DevOps and performance optimization.

However, independent benchmarks have raised questions about the model's performance. Researcher Elliot Arledge ran K2.7-Code against K2.6 and Claude Fable 5 on KernelBench-Hard, a public benchmark focused on GPU kernel optimization, and found mixed results.
